Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: 40-year-old woman with atopic history (childhood asthma, seasonal hay fever) presenting with 2 days of wheeze and dyspnea after dust exposure, worse at night, occasionally limiting speech. No chest pain or dizziness. Has not used inhaler during this episode.
- Differential diagnoses aligned with transcript:
  - Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by dust/allergen exposure (high likelihood): Atopic history, nocturnal worsening, wheeze, clear trigger, prior steroid use.
  - Irritant-induced bronchospasm from dust exposure (moderate likelihood): Temporal relationship to heavy dust; no infectious symptoms.
  - Allergic rhinitis with lower-airway involvement (moderate likelihood): Atopy and dust exposure; nasal/ocular symptoms not reported.
- Working diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation likely triggered by dust/allergen exposure.
- Management priorities: Urgent in-person assessment for objective measures (oxygen saturation, airway assessment) and to guide need for bronchodilator and/or oral steroids; consider antihistamine if allergic component.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions/recommendations:
  - Attend local clinic/GP today for assessment, including oxygen saturation measurement (pulse oximetry) and further evaluation.
  - Consider OTC antihistamine prior to visit if accessible; if not, GP can prescribe.
  - Possible need for oral steroids to be determined after in-person assessment.
  - Clinician to send a summary letter to GP; in-person consult expected to be brief (~10 minutes).
- Follow-up: In-person GP/clinic visit today as above. No other follow-up recorded.
- Patient education: Discussed that symptoms may be due to asthma or allergy; objective testing required before prescribing steroids.
- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): Not recorded.
- CTG registration: Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute asthma exacerbation triggered by dust/allergen exposure — Likelihood: High. Justification: Atopic history, onset after dust exposure, nocturnal worsening, wheeze, speech-limiting dyspnea, prior steroid use.
- Irritant-induced bronchospasm from dust/cleaning exposure — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Clear temporal link to heavy dust; no infectious prodrome.
- Allergic rhinitis with lower-airway involvement — Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Atopy and dust exposure consistent; absence of nasal symptoms reduces certainty.
